properties.decision:
ACCEPTED by Anthony, 2026-08-17. All three parts, with part (3) settled narrowly.

(1) `DEFAULT_SCOPE_DEPTH` becomes 2. At 3 the scoped detectors do not narrow: measured over all 56 Components of reflow2's own design, each returns 50-60 of the 83 gaps (median 55) and a region of 595-903 nodes. At 2 the same sweep returns 2-27 (median 4) over regions of 267-601. See `fact:defect-a-scoped-detector-at-its-default-depth-returns-two-thirds-of-the-design`.

WHY 2 AND NOT 1, which is the part the measurement alone does not settle. The golden thread runs Requirement -> Capability -> Component -> Artifact -> Verification. From a Component its capabilities are one hop; the requirements they satisfy and the checks that verify them are two. So depth 2 is exactly one component's own thread. Depth 1 stops short of the requirements, so a team would stop being told when its own capability satisfies nothing. Depth 3 reaches the neighbours' threads, which is the program again.

(2) The docstring that justifies 3 is corrected. It argues the third hop is needed to reach 'a contained child component's capabilities' — but `scope_region` puts the whole containment closure into the seed set BEFORE taking the radius, so those capabilities are one hop from an owned node, not three. The reason given for the default is not a reason the code needs. This part needed nobody's permission and was always going to be done.

(3) `detect_gaps`' description stops claiming its region is 'the same computation claim_region uses ... so "my area" means one thing everywhere'. SETTLED AS: DELETE THE SENTENCE. The alternative — actually reconciling `scope_region` and `claimed_region` — is NOT taken here and is NOT to be bundled in: it changes what a claim covers, which is what two people believe they have each taken responsibility for. That deserves its own decision, and `scope.rs` already records it as possibly a defect in the claims layer.
properties.name: The default scope depth drops from 3 to 2, and the two definitions of "a region" stop being described as one
properties.rationale:
ACCEPTED ON ANTHONY'S WORD after a plain-English walkthrough of all three parts with a recommendation on each.

WHAT WAS REJECTED. Leaving the default at 3 and telling callers to pass a depth: the measurement says the default is what almost everyone gets, and a tool whose out-of-the-box answer is 'two thirds of the design, called your part' fails the epoch this sits in. Also rejected: making `design_regions` quietly use a different depth from the scoped detectors, which would have hidden the defect behind a second opinion instead of naming it. Also rejected, and this is part (3): reconciling the two region computations as a rider on a default change.

HIS STANDING GROUND, restated the same day and applying directly here: 'I'm more interested in doing things right. If that requires redoing work, so be it - I prefer quality. So if adding SPECIFIES is right, then we have our answer regardless of the amount of work that it includes.' The cost of a correct change is not an argument against it before 1.0. See `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap`.

COST OF HAVING DECIDED LATER, kept on the record because the standing rule asks for it: every session that scoped between the measurement and this ruling was told its part held two thirds of the design's gaps, and any judgement made on that number — 'my area is the messy one' — was made on a figure that was the same for every area.
